source_refs.note: Book p. 49: 4.2.1 Addition of Matrices (conformable for addition, c_ij = a_ij + b_ij). The book gives no example here; the worked illustrations, Teaching notes, Key points and Common mistake are ours.

blocks.text: Matrix operations ka pehla aur sab se aasan amal: addition (jama). Is page ke baad aap kisi bhi do barabar order ki matrices ko pal bhar mein jama kar sakenge.
Kitab ki pehli baat: do matrices addition ke liye conformable (jama hone ke qabil) hoti hain agar un ka order same ho. Yani dono ki rows barabar hon aur dono ke columns bhi barabar hon.

Ab definition: do \(m \times n\) matrices \(A = [a_{ij}]\) aur \(B = [b_{ij}]\) ka jama \(A + B\) woh \(m \times n\) matrix \(C = [c_{ij}]\) hai jo \(A\) aur \(B\) ki corresponding (same position wali) entries ko jama karne se banti hai. Symbols mein hum \(C = A + B\) likhte hain, yani:

blocks.text_alt: c i j equals a i j plus b i j, entry by entry

blocks.text: jahan \(c_{ij} = a_{ij} + b_{ij}\), \(i = 1, 2, 3, \ldots, m;\ j = 1, 2, 3, \ldots, n\) ke liye. Is formula ko alfaaz mein parhiye: "jawab ki row \(i\), column \(j\) wali entry = \(A\) ki usi jagah wali entry + \(B\) ki usi jagah wali entry."

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: "Conformable" ka matlab hai "aapas mein jurne ke qabil". \(A\) ki har entry ko \(B\) mein usi jagah ek saathi chahiye. Socho do class ke result cards jin mein same subjects aur same students hon: un ko khana ba khana jama kar sakte hain. Lekin agar ek card mein 3 subjects hon aur doosre mein 4, to chautha subject kis se jama hoga? Isi liye order same hona shart hai. Aur jawab (sum) ka order bhi wahi hota hai jo \(A\) aur \(B\) ka hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Yeh hamari misaal hai, kitab ki nahin.
\[\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4\end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix}5 & -1 \\ 0 & 2\end{bmatrix}\]
Pehle order check: dono \(2 \times 2\), is liye jama ho sakta hai. Ab har position par jama karein:
\[= \begin{bmatrix} 1+5 & 2+(-1) \\ 3+0 & 4+2 \end{bmatrix}\]
\[= \begin{bmatrix}6 & 1 \\ 3 & 6\end{bmatrix}\]
Kyun: row 1, column 1 par \(1 + 5 = 6\); row 1, column 2 par \(2 + (-1) = 1\); row 2, column 1 par \(3 + 0 = 3\); row 2, column 2 par \(4 + 2 = 6\).
Tasdeeq: ulti tarteeb se jama karein, \(B + A\), to bhi har khane mein wahi jama aata hai, kyun ke \(5 + 1 = 1 + 5\). Yani \(A + B = B + A\); yeh property 4.3 mein aayegi.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Yeh jama define nahin: \(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 5 & 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix}\). Orders \(2 \times 2\) aur \(2 \times 3\) alag hain, is liye doosri matrix ke teesre column ka koi saathi nahin. Aise mein jawab "not defined" (mumkin nahin) likha jata hai; khali jagah par zero rakh kar jama karna ghalat hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
\(\begin{bmatrix} 2 & -3 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} -2 & 3 \end{bmatrix}\) kya hai?
Jawab: \(\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\), yani null matrix. Jab do matrices ki har entry ek doosre ki ulti (negative) ho to jama null matrix aata hai, bilkul jaise \(5 + (-5) = 0\).

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(A + B\) sirf tab define hai jab \(A\) aur \(B\) ka order same ho.
2. Same position wali entries jama karein: \(c_{ij} = a_{ij} + b_{ij}\).
3. Jawab ka order wahi hota hai jo \(A\) aur \(B\) ka hai.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Alag order ki matrices ko jama kar dena, ya khali jagah zero se bhar dena. Aisa jama define hi nahin.
2. Ghalat position ki entries jama karna, jaise \(A\) ki row ko \(B\) ke column se. Bachne ka tareeqa: ungli rakh kar dono matrices mein same khana dhoondiye.
3. Negative signs kho dena: \(2 + (-1) = 1\) hai, 3 nahin. Har negative entry ko bracket mein likhiye.
